question: Which of the following is the respiratory organ in earthworms?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Skin**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The respiratory organ in earthworms is their skin. Earthworms breathe through their skin by diffusion, which means that oxygen and carbon dioxide pass through their skin. 
 
• Here are some other things to know about earthworm respiration:
 
• Earthworms need to keep their skin moist to breathe.
 
• Air dissolves in the mucus on their skin, and if they dry out, they suffocate. 
 
• Earthworms have porous skin that allows air to pass through easily. 
 
• The moisture in the soil, mucus from epidermal gland cells, and coelomic fluid from dorsal pores all help keep an earthworm's skin moist. 
 
• When an earthworm takes in fresh air through its skin, oxygen is drawn into its circulatory system.
 
• The earthworm's heart then pumps the oxygenated blood to its head. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Spiracles
 
• Insects breathe in through external openings called spiracles.
 
• These openings lead to a network of tubes called tracheae, which deliver oxygen to the insect's cells and remove carbon dioxide. 
 
• Gill pouches
 
• Lampreys and hagfish have gills in spherical pouches with circular openings.
 
• Each pouch contains two gills. 
 
• Lungs (air sacs)
 
• The lungs contain air sacs called alveoli, where oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged between the lungs and blood.
 
• The right lung has three lobes, and the left lung has two.
 
• The left lung is slightly smaller than the right because the heart takes up some space on the left side
